TLDR: Never knew my passion. Wanting to study abroad. Bad financial situation so took drop to prepare for jee. Wasted the whole year cause of ADHD. Feeling dumb and seld esteem has taken a big hit.


I was never interested in jee even after knowing those high packages. It was only after half of my 12th passed i realised that i really need to earn as soon as possible cause of my family conditions so i chose engineering. But supposedly i have ADHD and my mental health wasnt already great that i lost my focus completed and started to procrastinate like crazy emded up wasting the drop year. I feel like ive forgotten what i studied in 12th. It hurts to see how far ive come but still feeling stuck. The girl who used to top classes is now rotting in bed everything crying cause of the wasted potential. I probably womt go to any top engg college. Nor do i have the enough money to pay the tuitions. Have thought to apply for scholarships. I love law. But i decided go not pursue it cause of all the corruption i see everyday. I thought is it even worth it to study law in india and the starting salary is less and got so blinded by those high packages of NITs. But now i realise theres a lot i could've done to live a life the way i wanted. Now cant really get a good rank in CLAT. and also not sure if i can get a good college for CSE. I have decided to just work till 30 or 35 and then go for masters and phd abroad. 
Its because i made some unrealistic goals for myself. I hope i can soon save up some money and go to therapy.

In the UK, most high-school students finishing their last year of school spend 1 week in a career place(s) of their choice. It could be a hospital, solicitor's office or a restaurant kitchen. The entire week, they spend 9-5 shadowing the staff to observe and see if this is something they want as a career before applying for the relevant course in Universities. It's called work shadowing.
I was very passionate To hoin the legal fraternity. I visited District court for a week in 2012, later i realised its not what I expected. Its always a good idea to have a trail.
